No external cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit have been established [DharmaNexus]. However, computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, detecting 64 matching passages across 15 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The poem shares significant portions with commentarial literature, including the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* and both parts of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, repetitive stock formulas—particularly across segments 6.1–9.1—are shared with multiple other Therāpadāna poems, most notably the *Padīpadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 266), *Saccasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 215), *Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 130), *Ekasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 216), and *Buddhasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 119) [DharmaNexus].
